content: Bromine monochloride, also known as bromine(I) chloride, bromochloride, or bromine chloride, is an interhalogen inorganic compound with the chemical formula BrCl. It exists as an unstable red-brown gas with a boiling point of 5°C and a melting point of -66°C. Its CAS number is 13863-41-7, and its EINECS number is 237-601-4. Bromine monochloride is a potent oxidizing agent. In analytical chemistry, bromine monochloride is utilized to detect trace levels of mercury. It achieves this by quantitatively oxidizing mercury in a sample to its Hg(II) state. Additionally, bromine monochloride serves as a biocide, specifically functioning as an algaecide, fungicide, and disinfectant. It is commonly employed in industrial recirculating cooling water systems. For example, it is the active ingredient in biocidal products such as Stabrom 909. Furthermore, bromine monochloride is added to certain types of lithium-sulfur dioxide (Li-SO2) batteries to enhance their voltage and energy density.
